payload.question_text: What can networking tools connect? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Retaining files is a storage responsibility. Networking is concerned with communication and connections.
options.better_fit: Choose this when files need to be saved and managed.

feedback.intrinsic: This would turn a data-retention task into a connection task.
feedback.instructional: Storage retains files; networking connects resources.

options.rationale: Correct. Networking connects cloud resources to each other. It supports secure, efficient communication between them.
Correct. Networking can connect cloud resources to the internet. Internet connectivity is one of its roles.
Correct. Networking can connect cloud resources to an organization. It supports efficient communication across that boundary.

payload.explanation: Correct. Networking connects cloud resources to each other, the internet, and organizations.

options.text: A collection of services used over the internet
options.rationale: Correct. A cloud platform provides a collection of services through the internet. It avoids requiring an organization to run everything on owned servers.
This describes compute rather than a whole cloud platform. Compute is one service category for running workloads.
options.better_fit: Choose this when an application needs capacity to run in the cloud.

feedback.intrinsic: This would identify only one service category.
feedback.instructional: A cloud platform includes compute and other internet-delivered services.

options.text: A managed platform for hosting applications
options.rationale: This describes App Services rather than the overall platform. App Services are one category within a cloud platform.
options.better_fit: Choose this when a team wants managed application hosting.

feedback.intrinsic: This would make the platform seem narrower than it is.
feedback.instructional: App Services are part of a broader cloud platform.

options.text: A service for retaining files and backups
options.rationale: This describes storage rather than a cloud platform. Storage is one category for saving and managing data.
options.better_fit: Choose this when files, databases, or backups must remain available.

feedback.intrinsic: This would omit the platform's other capabilities.
feedback.instructional: Storage is a service category within the larger platform.

payload.explanation: Correct. A cloud platform is a collection of services delivered through the internet.

payload.question_text: Networking helps cloud resources communicate securely and efficiently.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This could cause a team to overlook its connectivity needs.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Networking securely and efficiently connects cloud resources.

payload.explanation: Correct. Secure, efficient communication is networking's role.

payload.question_text: Azure is a cloud platform for building secure, reliable applications that can scale globally.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Marking this false could exclude Azure from a global application plan.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Azure is a cloud platform for building secure, reliable applications that can scale globally.

payload.explanation: Correct. Azure supports secure, reliable applications at global scale.

payload.question_text: Which statements describe compute? Select all that apply.

options.text: It runs applications in the cloud
options.rationale: Correct. Compute provides capacity for running applications. Running cloud workloads is its central role.
Correct. Programs and workloads use compute capacity. Compute supplies the cloud resources that execute them.
Saving files and backups is storage's role. Compute runs work instead of providing persistent data retention.
options.better_fit: Choose this when data must remain available later.

feedback.intrinsic: This would assign a data-retention need to running capacity.
feedback.instructional: Storage keeps data, while compute runs workloads.

options.text: It provides managed app hosting without server management
options.rationale: Managed application hosting is the role of App Services. Compute is cloud capacity rather than a ready-made hosting platform.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the team wants to host an app without managing servers.

feedback.intrinsic: This would obscure the distinction between capacity and managed hosting.
feedback.instructional: Compute runs workloads; App Services provide managed application platforms.

payload.explanation: Correct. Compute supplies cloud capacity for running applications, programs, and workloads.

payload.question_text: Which category saves and manages cloud data?

options.rationale: Compute runs applications and workloads. It is not the category for persistent cloud data.
options.better_fit: Choose this when an application or workload must run in the cloud.

feedback.intrinsic: This could leave data without a place to persist.
feedback.instructional: Storage retains data; compute runs work.

options.rationale: Networking connects cloud resources securely and efficiently. It does not save or manage cloud data.
options.better_fit: Choose this when resources need secure connections.

feedback.intrinsic: A connection would not provide persistent data management.
feedback.instructional: Networking handles communication; storage handles data.

options.rationale: Correct. Storage saves and manages cloud data. It keeps that data accessible later.
App Services provide managed application hosting. They do not identify the category for retaining cloud data.
options.better_fit: Choose this when hosting an application without managing servers.

feedback.intrinsic: The app could be hosted while the data need remains unresolved.
feedback.instructional: App Services host applications; storage keeps their data.

payload.explanation: Correct. Storage keeps cloud data available for later use.

payload.question_text: Compute is mainly used to save and manage files, databases, and backups.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Treating compute as storage could leave data without persistent retention.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Compute runs applications and workloads; storage saves files, databases, and backups.

payload.explanation: Correct. Storage saves and manages cloud data.

payload.question_text: Storage services primarily connect cloud resources to the internet.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This could send a connectivity need to the wrong service category.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Storage manages data, while networking connects resources to the internet and each other.

payload.explanation: Correct. Networking is responsible for connecting resources to the internet.

payload.question_text: What does a production AI application need besides a model? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Production AI applications need security around their users, data, and services. A model alone does not provide that protection.
Correct. Production AI applications need networking for their connections. The model alone is not the complete operational system.
A model catalog can help select a model but is not a complete production application. Security, networking, hosting, scaling, storage, logic, and a user interface are also needed.
options.better_fit: Choose this when browsing or evaluating available models.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could select a model but still lack a secure, usable application.
feedback.instructional: A model is one component; production delivery needs supporting infrastructure and application components.

options.rationale: Correct. Applications need storage for data they save and retrieve. This is infrastructure around the model.

payload.explanation: Correct. Production AI apps need supporting capabilities around a model.

payload.question_text: What are ready-made platforms for building and hosting apps without managing servers?

options.error_type: Confuses managed platforms with cloud computers
options.rationale: Compute supplies cloud capacity for workloads. It does not itself provide managed application hosting.
options.better_fit: Choose this when a workload needs cloud computer capacity.

feedback.intrinsic: The team may still need to manage more of the hosting environment.
feedback.instructional: Compute is capacity; App Services are managed app platforms.

options.error_type: Confuses app hosting with saved data
options.rationale: Storage saves and manages data. It does not host applications as ready-made platforms do.
options.better_fit: Choose this when application data must be retained.

feedback.intrinsic: The app's data could be kept while its hosting need remains open.
feedback.instructional: Storage handles data; App Services handle managed hosting.

options.rationale: Networking securely connects resources. It does not provide a ready-made platform for applications.
options.better_fit: Choose this when resources need secure communication.

feedback.intrinsic: Resources may connect while the app still lacks a hosting platform.
feedback.instructional: Networking handles connections; App Services handle app hosting.

options.rationale: Correct. App Services are ready-made platforms for building and hosting applications. They remove underlying server-management work.

payload.explanation: Correct. App Services provide ready-made platforms for applications.

payload.question_text: A production AI application needs only a model because Azure removes the need for security and storage.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This could leave an AI app without essential protections and data capabilities.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Azure provides services for security and storage, but production applications still need those capabilities.

payload.explanation: Correct. A model alone is not a complete production application.

payload.question_text: App Services let teams build, host, and run applications without managing the underlying servers.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This could cause a team to overlook a managed hosting option.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: App Services are ready-made platforms for building, hosting, and running applications without server management.

payload.explanation: Correct. Avoiding underlying server management is a key App Services benefit.
